ordinaryCallerFacts.fact: The ordinary JavaScriptExecuteRequest executes the authored native ClassicScript Program in the document main world and, when a result is requested, creates the platform WebV8ValueConverter, sets DateAllowed=true and RegExpAllowed=true, then calls GetJavaScriptExecutionResult.

GetJavaScriptExecutionResult calls converter.FromV8Value exactly once for a nonempty completion. If conversion yields nullptr, the ordinary return is base::Value() (null), which the shown Android callback serializes to raw null text.

This ordinary caller does not set FunctionAllowed, StripNullFromObjects, ConvertNegativeZeroToInt or Strategy. Under the bound converter constructor these remain false/false/false/null; Date and RegExp must not be treated as constructor defaults.

With the explicitly requested DateAllowed=true, the bound converter turns Date into ValueOf()/1000.0 (seconds as a double), not JSON.stringify ISO text. RegExpAllowed=true returns its string representation, not an empty object. Both belong in WK native information-preservation characterization.
Plain ordinary execution does not use the ForTests resolve_promises setting or an async-function wrapper. No Promise-resolution contract is inferred from the neighboring test-only method.

facts.fact: Android Java callback receives base::WriteJson(base::Value).value_or(""). It is not page JSON.stringify or preservation of page property insertion order.
WriteJson calls JSONWriter::Write, which calls WriteWithOptions with options=0. No pretty print, no omit-binary or omit-double-type-preservation flags are set.

DictValue owns flat_map<string, unique_ptr<Value>>, and its bulk constructor explicitly describes sorting. JSONWriter iterates this dictionary directly. Source-derived result order is sorted string-key order, not ECMAScript own-property insertion order. UTF8 string comparison is relevant; no Swift canonical Unicode key merging is permitted.

The converter tests IsInt32 before generic Number. Values represented as Int32 serialize as integer; ordinary 1.0 is not generally forced to 1.0. Finite values outside that representation enter the double branch; nonfinite numbers return nullptr.

With default flags, NumberToString(double) receives a .0 suffix only if no decimal/exponent occurs in its output. For example an integral double outside Int32 such as 2147483648 has a serialization boundary different from JavaScript JSON.stringify. Full shortest-double, escaping and negative-zero parity are not established by a Foundation JSON implementation.

Under the shown default converter, undefined/function/nonfinite produce nullptr and object properties with nullptr children are omitted. Arrays substitute null instead. Function-allowed and other converter flags are configurable and the actual rendering caller flags remain outside this four-file scope.

Object conversion enumerates own property names and reads each member. A member named toJSON is an ordinary member; no toJSON protocol is called by this algorithm. A function-valued member is skipped under default function_allowed=false.

A throwing object getter is caught and its child becomes V8 null; JSON.stringify instead propagates the exception. Prewalking followed by stringify would read observable getters twice and remains rejected.

A cycle detected by ScopedUniquenessGuard becomes base null. An API wrapper/DOM object becomes an empty dictionary in this converter. Date, RegExp, function, ArrayBuffer and strategy switches differ; Promise behavior and actual caller settings are not guessed.

Default JSONWriter refuses a binary value instead of JSON.stringify-style object conversion. WriteJson failure becomes empty callback text at the shown Android callback. A page typed-array/ArrayBuffer path therefore cannot be approved merely because stringify returns a string.

priorMAINFilesReassessment.priorNarrowFactStillValid: The WebKit scripting MAIN-files route executes a native page Program but completion has already crossed Foundation id, is JSON-encoded and reparsed before extension result delivery. It cannot promise retention of JavaScript insertion order.
priorMAINFilesReassessment.priorExclusionNowInsufficient: Insertion-order retention is not the demonstrated Android callback target. Consequently that exclusion must not be used as proof that MAIN-files, or existing native Program evaluateJavaScript, cannot implement the required result contract.
priorMAINFilesReassessment.smallerNextProductionRoute: Reassess the existing native evaluateJavaScript Program callback before adding extension machinery. If its native object projection can supply the required information, construct a bounded explicit Android-compatible value tree and deterministic base-dictionary JSON writer off main, then feed the existing JVM raw callback policy once. Preserve Program, global bindings, task ownership and cancellation.
remainingRequiredCharacterization: Does WK native NSDictionary/NSArray projection omit or conflate undefined/function/nonfinite values?
Are getter exceptions/cycles/Date/RegExp/API wrappers/typed arrays observable or already irreversibly converted?
Can native key enumeration retain both raw UTF16-distinct canonically equivalent names? Avoid bridging to Swift Dictionary<String,...> before testing.
Can Int32 vs double, negative zero, large finite doubles and exact escaping be reproduced?
Does current pending ordered characterization pass only prove captured JSON behavior rather than Android conversion parity? Yes: it must not be used as Android approval.
